rule: The page never scrolls. The app fills the window. A panel may scroll inside itself.
why: A scrolling page hides the pipeline and breaks on a phone.

rule: Below the compact width, show one pane at a time. Keep the pane switch in a dock at the bottom.
why: The thumb reaches the bottom edge. The three panes do not fit side by side.

rule: Make every tap target at least the touch size on a narrow window.
why: Small targets cause missed taps with gloves and on a bench.

rule: Use one accent colour. It marks the bridge, the active step and the one primary action.
why: One accent tells the reader where to look.

rule: Set labels in the mono face, 10 to 11 px, uppercase, with 0.1 to 0.16 em tracking. Set body text in the sans face at 13 px.
why: Mono labels read as instrument markings. Sans text stays easy to read.

rule: Build the page as drafting paper: cream sheet, fine grid and ink lines. Make cards lighter than the sheet.
why: The look says engineering, not marketing.

rule: Use motion to explain a change: a line arrives, a step finishes. Use the motion tokens. Stop motion when the user asks for reduced motion.
why: Motion that explains is useful. Other motion distracts.

rule: Show a state with a word or an icon as well as a colour.
why: Some readers cannot tell the colours apart.

rule: Write no raw colour, radius, shadow or timing in a stylesheet. Use a token.
why: One source means one change. A test enforces this.

rule: Run the fit check after every layout change. It opens every window size in the viewports file.
why: A layout that fits one size often fails another.
